newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile central bank to swap bank debt for equity.
newsitem.headline: Chile central bank to swap bank debt for equity.

text.p: Chile's central bank said on Wednesday it reached agreement over the repayment of debt owed by the Banco de Santiago, clearing the way for its long-awaited merger with Banco O'Higgins.
Under the terms of the deal with the bank's owners, O'Higgins Central Hispanoamericano SA, the central bank will take control of 38.5 percent of the merged bank in payment of $1.75 billion in debt.
In addition, the bank's owners have agreed to spend at least $130 million to buy some of the shares in the new entity from central bank, it said in a statement.
The deal is subject to approval by regulators and the shareholders of both banks involved in the merger, it said.
Santiago and O'Higgins, two of Chile's largest private banks, are controlled by the Luksic group.
The pact is one of the last in a series of deals to clear debt owed by private banks to the central bank, which bailed them out during a financial crisis in the early 1980s.

"The Chilean central bank is satisfied by the deal which it considers important not only for its interests and those of the banks involved, but also for the financial sector and the country in general," said the statement.
